texts: State was living in random variables. Refresh the page and everybody’s cart vanished.
Installed whatever package shut the error up. No idea what half of them do.
Skipped auth completely. “It’s just a prototype” is my favourite security policy.
Architecture? Bro I just kept regenerating until the errors stopped screaming.
Had zero way of knowing why it broke… until it broke live on stage.
Was just happy it produced *a* result. Correct result was optional.
Built the whole thing for one player and prayed multiplayer would appear by magic.
Stored whatever random data the API spat out. Schema? That’s corporate talk.
Only tested the perfect path. Real users? That’s their problem, not mine.
Let random packages decide the tech stack. Intentional design? Never met her.
Completely ignored what happens when the WiFi drops mid-use. Chaos incoming.
Celebrated hard because it ran on my laptop. Deployment was a tomorrow problem.
FREE
Assumed concurrency was for “real” apps, not our little app thing.
Kept saying “AI can just regenerate it” every time the code looked cursed.
Built the most generic app ever and hoped uniqueness would show up later.
Testing strategy: “I clicked it a few times and it looked cute.”
Told the AI “just make the button work” and acted shocked when the whole app had no logic.
Cared more about looking clever than making the actual rules correct.
Skipped every trade-off conversation because the deadline was breathing down my neck.
Tested with 4 users. Scaling to a room full of people felt like overthinking.
Took the first thing that worked and called it innovation.
Added logs only after the demo crashed in front of the judges. Classic.
“It works on my machine” was the entire deployment strategy.
Refused to look at existing apps so I could “stay original.” Ended up basic.
